title: Effective Dates of Memory Care Program Changes and the Split Month
content:
Under the Memory Care Residency Agreement a change of care program does not always take effect on the day of the assessment that finds it. The effective date depends on the direction of the change and on the type of reassessment, and a change in the middle of a month splits that month's rate charge.

## The rule

1. A move to a higher program found at a change of condition or post-hospital reassessment takes effect on the assessment date.
2. A move to a higher program found at a routine or post-move-in reassessment may be recorded only once the program increase notice period has passed since the written program notice was issued. The notice period is counted in calendar days from the notice date, the notice date being day 0, and the change takes effect on the day the count reaches the program increase notice period. That period is 30 calendar days on every tier. The notice date is the one recorded with the assessment.
3. A move to a lower program takes effect on the first day of the month following the assessment, whatever the type of reassessment.
4. A mid-month change splits the month's rate charge at the effective date; days already billed at the higher rate are returned as a program change proration credit referencing the original charge, each amount rounded to the cent half up. A prorated amount is the monthly rate of the tier billed multiplied by the days billed and divided by the days in that calendar month, rounded once to the cent, half up.

## Effective date by reassessment type and direction

| Reassessment type | Higher program | Lower program |
|---|---|---|
| Change of condition | The assessment date | First day of the following month |
| Post-hospital | The assessment date | First day of the following month |
| Routine | Day 30 counted from the written program notice (notice date is day 0) | First day of the following month |
| Post-move-in | Day 30 counted from the written program notice (notice date is day 0) | First day of the following month |

## Notice period boundary (hypothetical dates)

Written program notice issued on 4 June after a routine reassessment that found a higher program.

| Date | Count from the notice date | Higher program may be recorded |
|---|---|---|
| 3 July | 29 | No |
| 4 July | 30 | Yes - this is the effective date |

## Split month: worked figure (hypothetical rates)

A higher program takes effect on 21 November (a 30-day month). The earlier tier's hypothetical rate is 7000.00 and the new tier's hypothetical rate is 8000.00.

| Span | Days billed | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| 1 to 20 November, earlier tier | 20 | 7000.00 multiplied by 20, divided by 30: 4666.67 |
| 21 to 30 November, new tier | 10 | 8000.00 multiplied by 10, divided by 30: 2666.67 |

Each amount is rounded on its own to the cent, half up (4666.666... to 4666.67, 2666.666... to 2666.67).

## Points of judgement

- A higher program found at a change of condition reassessment on 14 May is billed from 14 May; the same finding at a routine reassessment with its notice issued on 14 May is billed from 13 June, the 30th day of the count.
- A lower program found on any date in May takes effect on 1 June.
